basis_statement: Preview, print, download, and externalized delivery remain context-bound affordances. They cannot be widened from raw storage location, bare route state, or stale cache identity alone.

source_lineage.rationale: Security law requires delivery reuse to stay bound to current route, access, and masking context.
Cache isolation already binds object, route, masking, and delivery context, which the delivery policy must reuse.
Customer-facing preview and export affordances must always reflect the current artifact meaning.
Edge policy already distinguishes signed delivery and binding requirements for cacheable versus no-store surfaces.

forbidden_shortcuts: storage_ref as iframe or image src
reuse of stale preview handle after route change
route token without canonical object identity
lawful_examples: current artifact preview target plus delivery_binding_hash
selected historical preview target plus delivery_binding_hash
notes: Previews remain route-bound and object-bound so stale tabs cannot widen access.
Current preview defaults and explicit history preview selection remain separate states.

forbidden_shortcuts: signed URL treated as durable ref
delivery handle reused across masking posture changes
lawful_examples: customer-safe derivative download_ref minted from a source artifact ref
notes: Download handles are disposable and may not masquerade as durable refs.
A download route must fail closed when its binding hash no longer matches current context.

forbidden_shortcuts: browser print of raw storage URL
reuse of preview cache key as print binding
lawful_examples: print target ref plus delivery binding
current artifact print target rebinding after access-step-up
notes: Print remains a sibling affordance to preview and download, not a fallback from either.

forbidden_shortcuts: sharing download_ref across tenant or visibility partitions
embedding external signed URL into durable contracts
lawful_examples: governed export target plus externalization-specific delivery binding
notes: Externalized delivery remains a governed derivative surface and may require additional visibility partitioning.
